sanskrit: naravānararājau tau sa ca vāyusutaḥ kapiḥ jāmbavān ṛkṣarājaś ca rākṣasaś ca vibhīṣaṇaḥ
english: Those two kings, of men and monkeys, and Hanūmat the son of the Wind, Jāmbavān king of the bears, and Vibhīṣaṇa the rākṣasa —

sanskrit: aṅgado vāliputraś ca saumitriḥ śarabhaḥ kapiḥ suṣeṇaḥ sahadāyādo maindo dvivida eva ca
english: Aṅgada son of Vālin, Lakṣmaṇa son of Sumitrā, the monkey Śarabha, Suṣeṇa with his kinsmen, and Mainda and Dvivida —

sanskrit: gajo gavākṣo kumudo nalo 'tha panasas tathā amitraviṣayaṃ prāptāḥ samavetāḥ samarthayan
english: Gaja, Gavākṣa, Kumuda, Nala, and Panasa — having reached the territory of the enemy, they assembled and deliberated.

sanskrit: iyaṃ sā lakṣyate laṅkā purī rāvaṇapālitā sāsuroragagandharvair amarair api durjayā
english: "This is that Laṅkā, seen before us now, the city guarded by Rāvaṇa — unconquerable even by asuras, serpents, gandharvas, and the immortal gods."

sanskrit: kāryasiddhiṃ puraskṛtya mantrayadhvaṃ vinirṇaye nityaṃ saṃnihito hy atra rāvaṇo rākṣasādhipaḥ
english: "With success of our mission as the foremost aim, deliberate and reach a firm resolve, for Rāvaṇa, lord of rākṣasas, is ever present here within."

sanskrit: tathā teṣu bruvāṇeṣu rāvaṇāvarajo 'bravīt vākyam agrāmyapadavat puṣkalārthaṃ vibhīṣaṇaḥ
english: While they were speaking thus, Vibhīṣaṇa, younger brother of Rāvaṇa, spoke words refined in diction and rich in meaning:

sanskrit: analaḥ śarabhaś caiva saṃpātiḥ praghasas tathā gatvā laṅkāṃ mamāmātyāḥ purīṃ punar ihāgatāḥ
english: "Anala, Śarabha, Saṃpāti, and Praghasa — my ministers — went to the city of Laṅkā and have now returned here."

sanskrit: bhūtvā śakunayaḥ sarve praviṣṭāś ca ripor balam vidhānaṃ vihitaṃ yac ca tad dṛṣṭvā samupasthitāḥ
english: "Disguising themselves as birds, they all entered the enemy's forces, observed every arrangement that had been made, and then came back."

sanskrit: saṃvidhānaṃ yathāhus te rāvaṇasya durātmanaḥ rāma tad bruvataḥ sarvaṃ yathātathyena me śṛṇu
english: "O Rāma, hear from me all the dispositions of that evil-souled Rāvaṇa exactly as they have reported them:"

sanskrit: pūrvaṃ prahastaḥ sabalo dvāram āsādya tiṣṭhati dakṣiṇaṃ ca mahāvīryau mahāpārśvamahodarau
english: "At the eastern gate, Prahasta stands in force. At the southern gate stand the two of great valor, Mahāpārśva and Mahodara."

sanskrit: indrajit paścimadvāraṃ rākṣasair bahubhir vṛtaḥ paṭṭasāsidhanuṣmadbhiḥ śūlamudgarapāṇibhiḥ
english: "Indrajit holds the western gate, surrounded by many rākṣasas bearing swords and bows, and carrying tridents and maces in their hands."

sanskrit: nānāpraharaṇaiḥ śūrair āvṛto rāvaṇātmajaḥ rākṣasānāṃ sahasrais tu bahubhiḥ śastrapāṇibhiḥ
english: "Rāvaṇa's son is surrounded by heroes armed with various weapons, and by many thousands of rākṣasas with weapons in hand."

sanskrit: yuktaḥ paramasaṃvigno rākṣasair bahubhir vṛtaḥ uttaraṃ nagaradvāraṃ rāvaṇaḥ svayam āsthitaḥ
english: "Alert and extremely vigilant, surrounded by many rākṣasas, Rāvaṇa himself has taken his post at the northern gate of the city."

sanskrit: virūpākṣas tu mahatā śūlakhaḍgadhanuṣmatā balena rākṣasaiḥ sārdhaṃ madhyamaṃ gulmam āsthitaḥ
english: "Virūpākṣa, with a great force of rākṣasas bearing tridents, swords, and bows, has taken up position at the central reserve."

sanskrit: etān evaṃvidhān gulmāṃl laṅkāyāṃ samudīkṣya te māmakāḥ sacivāḥ sarve śīghraṃ punar ihāgatāḥ
english: "Having observed all these guard-posts of this kind in Laṅkā, all my ministers swiftly returned here."

sanskrit: gajānāṃ ca sahasraṃ ca rathānām ayutaṃ pure hayānām ayute dve ca sāgrakoṭī ca rakṣasām
english: "In the city there are a thousand elephants, ten thousand chariots, twenty thousand horses, and more than a crore of rākṣasas."

sanskrit: vikrāntā balavantaś ca saṃyugeṣv ātatāyinaḥ iṣṭā rākṣasarājasya nityam ete niśācarāḥ
english: "These night-rangers are valiant and powerful, aggressive in battle, and are ever the favorites of the king of rākṣasas."

sanskrit: ekaikasyātra yuddhārthe rākṣasasya viśāṃ pate parivāraḥ sahasrāṇāṃ sahasram upatiṣṭhate
english: "O lord of the people, for each single rākṣasa in battle readiness, a retinue of a thousand thousand stands in attendance."

sanskrit: etāṃ pravṛttiṃ laṅkāyāṃ mantriproktaṃ vibhīṣaṇaḥ rāmaṃ kamalapatrākṣam idam uttaram abravīt
english: Having reported this intelligence of Laṅkā as related by his ministers, Vibhīṣaṇa then spoke this reply to lotus-eyed Rāma:

sanskrit: kuberaṃ tu yadā rāma rāvaṇaḥ pratyayudhyata ṣaṣṭiḥ śatasahasrāṇi tadā niryānti rākṣasāḥ
english: "O Rāma, when Rāvaṇa fought against Kubera, sixty hundred thousand rākṣasas marched out to battle."

sanskrit: parākrameṇa vīryeṇa tejasā sattvagauravāt sadṛśā yo 'tra darpeṇa rāvaṇasya durātmanaḥ
english: "He who equals Rāvaṇa the evil-souled in prowess, valor, energy, and the dignity of spirit — and matches him in pride —

sanskrit: atra manyur na kartavyo roṣaye tvāṃ na bhīṣaye samartho hy asi vīryeṇa surāṇām api nigrahe
english: "— let no anger be felt on this account; I do not mean to provoke or frighten you, for you are capable by your valor even of subduing the gods."

sanskrit: tad bhavāṃś caturaṅgeṇa balena mahatā vṛtaḥ vyūhyedaṃ vānarānīkaṃ nirmathiṣyasi rāvaṇam
english: "Therefore, surrounded by a great fourfold army, you shall array this monkey host and crush Rāvaṇa."

sanskrit: rāvaṇāvaraje vākyam evaṃ bruvati rāghavaḥ śatrūṇāṃ pratighātārtham idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: As Rāvaṇa's younger brother was speaking thus, Rāghava spoke these words with the purpose of repelling his enemies:

sanskrit: pūrvadvāre tu laṅkāyā nīlo vānarapuṃgavaḥ prahastaṃ pratiyoddhā syād vānarair bahubhir vṛtaḥ
english: "Let Nīla, foremost among monkeys, surrounded by many monkeys, be the combatant to oppose Prahasta at Laṅkā's eastern gate."

sanskrit: aṅgado vāliputras tu balena mahatā vṛtaḥ dakṣiṇe bādhatāṃ dvāre mahāpārśvamahodarau
english: "And Aṅgada son of Vālin, attended by a great force, shall press hard at the southern gate against Mahāpārśva and Mahodara."

sanskrit: hanūmān paścimadvāraṃ nipīḍya pavanātmajaḥ praviśatv aprameyātmā bahubhiḥ kapibhir vṛtaḥ
english: "Hanūmat, son of the Wind, of immeasurable soul, shall overwhelm the western gate and enter in, surrounded by many monkeys."

sanskrit: daityadānavasaṃghānām ṛṣīṇāṃ ca mahātmanām viprakārapriyaḥ kṣudro varadānabalānvitaḥ
english: "He who delights in outraging hosts of daityas, dānavas, and great-souled sages — that vile one, emboldened by the boon he has received —

sanskrit: parikrāmati yaḥ sarvāṃl lokān saṃtāpayan prajāḥ tasyāhaṃ rākṣasendrasya svayam eva vadhe dhṛtaḥ
english: "— who roams through all the worlds tormenting its creatures: against that lord of rākṣasas I myself am resolved for his slaying."

sanskrit: uttaraṃ nagaradvāram ahaṃ saumitriṇā saha nipīḍyābhipravekṣyāmi sabalo yatra rāvaṇaḥ
english: "I, together with Lakṣmaṇa son of Sumitrā, shall assault and enter the northern gate of the city with my full force, where Rāvaṇa stands."

sanskrit: vānarendraś ca balavān ṛkṣarājaś ca jāmbavān rākṣasendrānujaś caiva gulme bhavatu madhyame
english: "The mighty king of monkeys, Sugrīva, the king of bears Jāmbavān, and the younger brother of the lord of rākṣasas, Vibhīṣaṇa — let them remain at the central reserve."

sanskrit: na caiva mānuṣaṃ rūpaṃ kāryaṃ haribhir āhave eṣā bhavatu naḥ saṃjñā yuddhe 'smin vānare bale
english: "The monkeys must not assume human form in battle — let this be our distinguishing mark for the monkey forces in this war."

sanskrit: vānarā eva niścihnaṃ svajane 'smin bhaviṣyati vayaṃ tu mānuṣeṇaiva sapta yotsyāmahe parān
english: "Monkeys alone shall be the distinction recognized among our own people; but we seven shall fight the enemies in human form."

sanskrit: aham eva saha bhrātrā lakṣmaṇena mahaujasā ātmanā pañcamaś cāyaṃ sakhā mama vibhīṣaṇaḥ
english: "I myself, with my brother Lakṣmaṇa of great might — and this Vibhīṣaṇa, my friend, as the fifth of our own number —"

sanskrit: sa rāmaḥ kāryasiddhyartham evam uktvā vibhīṣaṇam suvelārohaṇe buddhiṃ cakāra matimān matim
english: Having spoken thus to Vibhīṣaṇa with the aim of accomplishing his purpose, wise Rāma formed the resolve to ascend Mount Suvela.

sanskrit: tatas tu rāmo mahatā balena pracchādya sarvāṃ pṛthivīṃ mahātmā prahṛṣṭarūpo 'bhijagāma laṅkāṃ kṛtvā matiṃ so 'rivadhe mahātmā
english: Then great-souled Rāma, covering all the earth with his mighty host, joyous in bearing and with his mind fixed on the slaying of the enemy, great-souled as he was, advanced toward Laṅkā.

sanskrit: sa tu kṛtvā suvelasya matim ārohaṇaṃ prati lakṣmaṇānugato rāmaḥ sugrīvam idam abravīt
english: Having resolved upon ascending Suvela, Rāma, followed by Lakṣmaṇa, spoke these words to Sugrīva:

sanskrit: vibhīṣaṇaṃ ca dharmajñam anuraktaṃ niśācaram mantrajñaṃ ca vidhijñaṃ ca ślakṣṇayā parayā girā
english: — and with gentle and excellent speech addressed Vibhīṣaṇa, that night-ranger who knows righteousness, who is devoted, learned in counsel, and skilled in procedure:

sanskrit: suvelaṃ sādhu śailendram imaṃ dhātuśataiś citam adhyārohāmahe sarve vatsyāmo 'tra niśām imām
english: "Let us all ascend this lord of mountains, Suvela, resplendent with a hundred minerals, and spend this night here."

sanskrit: laṅkāṃ cālokayiṣyāmo nilayaṃ tasya rakṣasaḥ yena me maraṇāntāya hṛtā bhāryā durātmanā
english: "And we shall survey Laṅkā, the abode of that rākṣasa, that evil-souled one who carried off my wife to bring about his own death."

sanskrit: yena dharmo na vijñāto na vṛttaṃ na kulaṃ tathā rākṣasyā nīcayā buddhyā yena tad garhitaṃ kṛtam
english: "By whom neither righteousness was understood, nor conduct, nor lineage — by whom, with the vile intellect of a rākṣasa, that censurable deed was done."

sanskrit: yasmin me vardhate roṣaḥ kīrtite rākṣasādhame yasyāparādhān nīcasya vadhaṃ drakṣyāmi rakṣasām
english: "At whose very mention my fury mounts, that most base of rākṣasas — on account of whose transgression I shall witness the destruction of the rākṣasas."

sanskrit: eko hi kurute pāpaṃ kālapāśavaśaṃ gataḥ nīcenātmāpacāreṇa kulaṃ tena vinaśyati
english: "For one who is in the grip of the noose of Time commits sin alone, and through that base one's self-wrought transgression, his entire lineage perishes."

sanskrit: evaṃ saṃmantrayann eva sakrodho rāvaṇaṃ prati rāmaḥ suvelaṃ vāsāya citrasānum upāruhat
english: Speaking thus in counsel, his anger directed at Rāvaṇa, Rāma climbed Suvela with its variegated peaks for his night's lodging.

sanskrit: pṛṣṭhato lakṣmaṇa cainam anvagacchat samāhitaḥ saśaraṃ cāpam udyamya sumahad vikrame rataḥ
english: Behind him Lakṣmaṇa followed, composed and attentive, raising his great bow with its arrow nocked, delighting in great feats of valor.

sanskrit: tam anvarohat sugrīvaḥ sāmātyaḥ savibhīṣaṇaḥ hanūmān aṅgado nīlo maindo dvivida eva ca
english: Sugrīva ascended after him, along with his ministers, and Vibhīṣaṇa; Hanūmat, Aṅgada, Nīla, Mainda, and Dvivida as well.

sanskrit: gajo gavākṣo gavayaḥ śarabho gandhamādanaḥ panasaḥ kumudaś caiva haro rambhaś ca yūthapaḥ
english: Gaja, Gavākṣa, Gavaya, Śarabha, Gandhamādana, Panasa, Kumuda, and the troop-leader Hara and Rambha —

sanskrit: ete cānye ca bahavo vānarāḥ śīghragāminaḥ te vāyuvegapravaṇās taṃ giriṃ giricāriṇaḥ adhyārohanta śataśaḥ suvelaṃ yatra rāghavaḥ
english: — these and many other monkeys, swift of movement, swift as the wind's rush, those frequenters of mountains, climbed by the hundreds Mount Suvela where Rāghava was.

sanskrit: te tv adīrgheṇa kālena girim āruhya sarvataḥ dadṛśuḥ śikhare tasya viṣaktām iva khe purīm
english: In no long time, having climbed the mountain on all sides, they saw the city on its summit, hanging as it were suspended in the sky.

sanskrit: tāṃ śubhāṃ pravaradvārāṃ prākāravaraśobhitā laṅkāṃ rākṣasasaṃpūrṇāṃ dadṛśur hariyūthapāḥ
english: The leaders of monkey troops saw Laṅkā, beautiful, with its magnificent gates, graced by its excellent ramparts, and filled with rākṣasas.

sanskrit: prākāracayasaṃsthaiś ca tathā nīlair niśācaraiḥ dadṛśus te hariśreṣṭhāḥ prākāram aparaṃ kṛtam
english: Those foremost among monkeys saw another wall formed by dark-bodied night-rangers stationed upon the battlements — a living rampart.

sanskrit: te dṛṣṭvā vānarāḥ sarve rākṣasān yuddhakāṅkṣiṇaḥ mumucur vipulān nādāṃs tatra rāmasya paśyataḥ
english: All the monkeys, seeing those rākṣasas eager for battle, let out mighty roars there in Rāma's sight.

sanskrit: tato 'stam agamat sūryaḥ saṃdhyayā pratirañjitaḥ pūrṇacandrapradīpā ca kṣapā samabhivartate
english: Then the sun set, flushed with the hues of dusk, and night drew near, lit by the full moon like a lamp.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa rāmo harivāhinīpatir vibhīṣaṇena pratinandya satkṛtaḥ salakṣmaṇo yūthapayūthasaṃvṛtaḥ suvela pṛṣṭhe nyavasad yathāsukham
english: Then Rāma, lord of the monkey host, greeted and honored by Vibhīṣaṇa, together with Lakṣmaṇa and surrounded by throngs of troop-leaders, rested comfortably on the crest of Suvela.

sanskrit: tāṃ rātrim uṣitās tatra suvele haripuṃgavāḥ laṅkāyāṃ dadṛśur vīrā vanāny upavanāni ca
english: Having passed that night there on Suvela, those mighty monkey heroes, those warriors, beheld the groves and gardens of Laṅkā.

sanskrit: samasaumyāni ramyāṇi viśālāny āyatāni ca dṛṣṭiramyāṇi te dṛṣṭvā babhūvur jātavismayāḥ
english: Even, pleasant, broad, and extensive — delightful to the eye — seeing them, they were filled with wonder.

sanskrit: campakāśokapuṃnāgasālatālasamākulā tamālavanasaṃchannā nāgamālāsamāvṛtā
english: Teeming with campaka, aśoka, puṃnāga, śāla, and palm trees, overhung with groves of tamāla, wrapped in garlands of nāga trees —

sanskrit: hintālair arjunair nīpaiḥ saptaparṇaiś ca puṣpitaiḥ tilakaiḥ karṇikāraiś ca paṭālaiś ca samantataḥ
english: — with hintāla and arjuna trees, nīpa, and flowering saptaparṇa, tilaka, karṇikāra, and pāṭalī on every side —

sanskrit: śuśubhe puṣpitāgraiś ca latāparigatair drumaiḥ laṅkā bahuvidhair divyair yathendrasyāmarāvatī
english: — Laṅkā shone splendid with trees whose boughs were in bloom, entwined with creepers, and adorned with many kinds of divine plants, like Indra's Amarāvatī.

sanskrit: vicitrakusumopetai raktakomalapallavaiḥ śādvalaiś ca tathā nīlaiś citrābhir vanarājibhiḥ
english: With variegated flowers, red and tender shoots, stretches of blue-green lawn, and colorful rows of forest trees —

sanskrit: gandhāḍhyāny abhiramyāṇi puṣpāṇi ca phalāni ca dhārayanty agamās tatra bhūṣaṇānīva mānavāḥ
english: — the trees there bore fragrant, beautiful flowers and fruits, wearing them like ornaments, as men do.

sanskrit: tac caitrarathasaṃkāśaṃ manojñaṃ nandanopamam vanaṃ sarvartukaṃ ramyaṃ śuśubhe ṣaṭpadāyutam
english: That forest, resembling Caitraratha, charming, comparable to Nandana, blooming in all seasons, lovely, swarming with bees, shone splendidly.

sanskrit: natyūhakoyaṣṭibhakair nṛtyamānaiś ca barhibhiḥ rutaṃ parabhṛtānāṃ ca śuśruve vananirjhare
english: The sound of natyūha and koyaṣṭibhaka birds, of dancing peacocks, and the call of cuckoos was heard near the forest waterfalls.

sanskrit: nityamattavihaṃgāni bhramarācaritāni ca kokilākulaṣaṇḍāni vihagābhirutāni ca
english: The groves, ever resonant with intoxicated birds, frequented by bees, filled with flocks of cuckoos, and resounding with the calls of birds —

sanskrit: bhṛṅgarājābhigītāni bhramaraiḥ sevitāni ca koṇālakavighuṣṭāni sārasābhirutāni ca
english: — sung over by bhrṅgarāja birds, attended by bumblebees, ringing with the cry of koṇālaka birds, and resonant with the calls of sārasa cranes —

sanskrit: viviśus te tatas tāni vanāny upavanāni ca hṛṣṭāḥ pramuditā vīrā harayaḥ kāmarūpiṇaḥ
english: — into those groves and gardens the monkey heroes, shape-changers at will, then entered, joyful and full of delight.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ praviśatāṃ tatra vānarāṇāṃ mahaujasām puṣpasaṃsargasurabhir vavau ghrāṇasukho 'nilaḥ
english: As those monkeys of great might entered there, a wind blew that was fragrant with the mingling of flowers, pleasant to the breath.

sanskrit: anye tu harivīrāṇāṃ yūthān niṣkramya yūthapāḥ sugrīveṇābhyanujñātā laṅkāṃ jagmuḥ patākinīm
english: But other troop-leaders, issuing from the bands of monkey heroes with Sugrīva's permission, advanced toward banner-bearing Laṅkā.

sanskrit: vitrāsayanto vihagāṃs trāsayanto mṛgadvipān kampayantaś ca tāṃ laṅkāṃ nādaiḥ svair nadatāṃ varāḥ
english: Those foremost among the roaring ones frightened the birds, terrified the deer and elephants, and shook Laṅkā itself with their war-cries.

sanskrit: kurvantas te mahāvegā mahīṃ cāraṇapīḍitām rajaś ca sahasaivordhvaṃ jagāma caraṇoddhatam
english: Those swift-moving ones caused the earth to tremble under the tread of their feet, and the dust raised by those feet leaped up into the sky all at once.

sanskrit: ṛkṣāḥ siṃhā varāhāś ca mahiṣā vāraṇā mṛgāḥ tena śabdena vitrastā jagmur bhītā diśo daśa
english: Bears, lions, wild boars, buffaloes, elephants, and deer, terrified by that noise, fled in panic in all ten directions.

sanskrit: śikharaṃ tu trikūṭasya prāṃśu caikaṃ divispṛśam samantāt puṣpasaṃchannaṃ mahārajatasaṃnibham
english: And one tall summit of Trikūṭa, touching the sky, carpeted all around with flowers, resembling great silver —

sanskrit: śatayojanavistīrṇaṃ vimalaṃ cārudarśanam ślakṣṇaṃ śrīman mahac caiva duṣprāpaṃ śakunair api
english: — a hundred yojanas in breadth, pure, beautiful to behold, smooth, magnificent, vast, and inaccessible even to birds —

sanskrit: manasāpi durārohaṃ kiṃ punaḥ karmaṇā janaiḥ niviṣṭā tatra śikhare laṅkā rāvaṇapālitā
english: — difficult to scale even in the mind, how much more so by human physical effort — upon that summit sat Laṅkā, guarded by Rāvaṇa.

sanskrit: sā purī gopurair uccaiḥ pāṇḍurāmbudasaṃnibhaiḥ kāñcanena ca sālena rājatena ca śobhitā
english: That city shone with tall gate-towers resembling white clouds, and with pillars of gold and silver.

sanskrit: prāsādaiś ca vimānaiś ca laṅkā paramabhūṣitā ghanair ivātapāpāye madhyamaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ padam
english: Adorned supremely with palaces and aerial mansions, Laṅkā resembled at the end of summer the middle realm of Viṣṇu, laden with rain-clouds.

sanskrit: yasyāṃ stambhasahasreṇa prāsādaḥ samalaṃkṛtaḥ kailāsaśikharākāro dṛśyate kham ivollikhan
english: Within it a palace adorned with a thousand pillars was visible, shaped like the peak of Kailāsa, soaring upward as if to pierce the sky.

sanskrit: caityaḥ sa rākṣasendrasya babhūva purabhūṣaṇam śatena rakṣasāṃ nityaṃ yaḥ samagreṇa rakṣyate
english: That sanctuary of the lord of rākṣasas was the ornament of the city, guarded at all times by a full hundred rākṣasas.

sanskrit: tāṃ samṛddhāṃ samṛddhārtho lakṣmīvāṃl lakṣmaṇāgrajaḥ rāvaṇasya purīṃ rāmo dadarśa saha vānaraiḥ
english: Rāma, elder brother of Lakṣmaṇa, possessing all prosperity, himself wealthy in purpose, beheld Rāvaṇa's city, rich and opulent, together with the monkeys.

sanskrit: tāṃ ratnapūrṇāṃ bahusaṃvidhānāṃ prāsādamālābhir alaṃkṛtāṃ ca purīṃ mahāyantrakavāṭamukhyāṃ dadarśa rāmo mahatā balena
english: Rāma beheld that city filled with jewels, of many elaborate arrangements, adorned with rows of palaces, its gates fortified with great siege-engines — and he beheld it with his mighty host.
